items.question: If a rating preview is shown on hover, should `onChange` fire for every hovered star?
items.answer: No. Keep the committed rating separate from the transient hover preview and normally fire `onChange` only when the user commits a rating, such as by click or the defined keyboard action. The contract must document this explicitly.
items.trap: Treating preview as committed state makes a pointer merely passing over the control change the user's selection and creates two competing meanings for the value.

items.question: Why are child indexes a poor identity for compound tabs?
items.answer: An index changes when tabs are inserted, removed, or reordered. Stable tab values preserve the relationship between a tab, its panel, and the selected value across those changes.
items.trap: An index can appear to work in a static demo, but it silently selects or labels a different tab after a dynamic update.

items.question: Can a reusable input start with `value={undefined}` and later receive a string?
items.answer: No. That changes it from uncontrolled to controlled. Normalize a controlled text value to a string such as `value ?? ''`, keep the mode stable for the component lifetime, and use `defaultValue` when the component is intentionally uncontrolled.
items.trap: Checking only whether a value is truthy misclassifies valid empty values and permits a mode switch, which React explicitly warns against.

items.question: What should a controlled checkbox read from the change event?
items.answer: Read `event.target.checked`, not `event.target.value`, and update the backing boolean synchronously. Use `checked`, not `value`, to control checkbox selection.
items.trap: The string `value` attribute is form data; it does not represent whether the checkbox is currently checked.

items.question: Is `aria-modal="true"` enough to make a dialog modal?
items.answer: No. The application must actually prevent interaction with content outside the dialog and visually obscure that content. Only then should the dialog claim modal semantics, alongside an accessible name and contained Tab sequence.
items.trap: ARIA describes behavior to assistive technologies; it does not itself block pointer, keyboard, or programmatic interaction with the page behind the dialog.

items.question: Should a listbox option receive DOM focus whenever the user presses Arrow Down in an editable combobox?
items.answer: Not for the listbox-popup model described here. Keep DOM focus on the input and expose the active option through `aria-activedescendant`; keep popup descendants out of the page Tab sequence.
items.trap: Moving DOM focus into every option can break text editing and does not match the APG model for a listbox popup controlled by an editable combobox.

items.question: Does aborting the previous request alone guarantee that stale results cannot win?
items.answer: No. Abort the old operation and also guard result application by request ownership or identity. An aborted operation should be ignored, while genuine non-abort failures should be surfaced.
items.trap: Cancellation is a mechanism for stopping an operation, not a substitute for a correctness check at the point where results update state.

items.question: Does virtualization mean rendering every row but hiding most of them with CSS?
items.answer: No. Windowing renders only a visible subset, with a small overscan, and recycles or replaces nodes outside that window. CSS visibility alone leaves the large DOM and its work in place.
items.trap: The performance benefit comes from reducing rendered DOM and rendering work, not merely from changing visual visibility.

items.question: Can a generic table safely infer whether Next is enabled from the current page number?
items.answer: Not without an API contract. Numbered pages may provide a total, while cursor-based APIs commonly provide a next-cursor or `hasNext` signal. The table should receive the relevant contract rather than inventing total-count behavior.
items.trap: A page number does not reveal whether another server page exists, especially when filtering or cursor pagination is involved.

items.question: After focus stops an auto-rotating carousel, may a timer automatically resume when focus leaves?
items.answer: No. The APG carousel guidance says rotation stops when focus enters and does not resume unless the user explicitly requests it through the rotation control. Hover should also stop rotation.
items.trap: Automatic resumption can change content while a user is trying to continue reading and removes the user's explicit control over rotation.

items.question: Can one shared focus trap be applied to both a modal and a combobox popup?
items.answer: No. Share mechanics such as focus restoration and cleanup, but keep pattern semantics separate. A modal contains the Tab sequence; a listbox combobox normally keeps DOM focus on the input and uses `aria-activedescendant`.
items.trap: A universal trap changes a combobox's text-editing and focus model, producing behavior that is wrong even if the utility works for dialogs.

items.question: Should every component state value be synchronized into the URL for Back-button support?
items.answer: No. Put user-meaningful, shareable feature state such as page, page size, and filters in the URL when deep linking and history matter. Keep transient state such as hover and pending rendering state local.
items.trap: Serializing ephemeral state pollutes browser history and makes the URL a second owner of details that do not represent a navigable view.

items.question: D3 is a chart library like Chart.js, just more powerful?
items.answer: No: D3 is primitives you compose; Chart.js is finished chart types on canvas.
items.trap: Choosing D3 for a standard chart means building what Chart.js ships by default.

mcqs.question: Which design gives a React text input a stable controlled mode when data may initially be missing?
options: Pass `value={apiValue}` and let it be undefined initially
Pass `value={apiValue ?? ''}` and update it synchronously in `onChange`
Pass both `value={apiValue}` and `defaultValue=''`
Use `defaultValue={apiValue}` and also mirror it into local state on every render
mcqs.explanation: A controlled text input needs a string value and a synchronous `onChange` update. The best distractor is option 1: allowing undefined first can change the input from uncontrolled to controlled. `value` and `defaultValue` are not two simultaneous ownership modes.

mcqs.question: What is the strongest reason to lift active-tab state into the Tabs owner?
options: It guarantees fewer React renders in every tree
It lets each tab keep an independent source of truth
It coordinates the tab and panel parts through one owner
It removes the need for stable tab identifiers
mcqs.explanation: React recommends moving shared state to the closest common parent so coordinated parts have one source of truth. Option 1 is wrong because lifting state is about coordination, not a blanket render optimization; option 4 is wrong because stable identity remains necessary.

mcqs.question: Which requirement is part of a genuinely modal dialog implementation?
options: Only add `aria-modal=true` to the dialog element
Leave the invoking button focused behind the dialog
Keep Tab and Shift+Tab within the dialog and restore focus on close
Make the backdrop the only way to close it
mcqs.explanation: The APG modal pattern contains the dialog's Tab sequence, moves focus inside on open, and normally returns focus to the invoker on close. Option 0 fails because ARIA does not implement inertness; option 3 excludes the required visible close-button pattern.

mcqs.question: For an editable combobox with a listbox popup, where does DOM focus normally remain while an option is highlighted?
options: On the highlighted `option` element
On the page body
On the input, with `aria-activedescendant` naming the active option
On every option simultaneously through roving tabindex
mcqs.explanation: The APG model maintains DOM focus on the combobox and communicates the active popup item with `aria-activedescendant`. Option 0 describes a different focus strategy and can interfere with editable text behavior.

mcqs.question: What should an async autocomplete clean up when its query changes?
options: Only the rendered suggestions
The debounce timer and the previous request, while ignoring abort errors
The input value, so the next request starts empty
Every request, including the newest request
mcqs.explanation: The bank's model cancels scheduled work and the in-flight request for the previous query, while real errors remain visible. Option 0 does not stop stale work, and option 3 would cancel the request needed for the current query.

mcqs.question: What is the primary performance mechanism of list virtualization?
options: Render all rows and set `display:none` on most rows
Render only the visible window plus limited overscan
Replace stable row keys with array indexes
Increase the overscan window until every row is mounted
mcqs.explanation: Windowing keeps only a small visible subset in the DOM, with overscan used to reduce blank flashes. Option 0 still pays the large-DOM cost, and option 3 defeats the purpose of virtualization.

mcqs.question: Which pagination rule is safe when filters change?
options: Keep the current page no matter what the new result set contains
Reset or clamp the page when the current page is no longer valid
Disable all pagination until the user reloads
Compute the next page from the row array index only
mcqs.explanation: Changing filters can reduce the result set, so the current page may become invalid and should be reset or clamped according to the contract. The other options either show an invalid page or ignore server pagination semantics.

mcqs.question: What must an auto-rotating carousel provide in addition to previous and next controls?
options: A rotation stop/start control and pause on focus and hover
A timer that resumes after every blur automatically
A hidden clickable backdrop instead of buttons
A requirement that all slides remain in the page Tab sequence
mcqs.explanation: The APG carousel pattern calls for a rotation control and stopping rotation on keyboard focus or pointer hover, without automatic resumption after focus. The other choices remove user control or add unnecessary tab stops.

mcqs.question: What is the right abstraction boundary for a shared focus-management primitive?
options: Encode dialog, combobox, and menu semantics in one universal component
Share mechanics such as restoration and cleanup, while adapters own widget semantics
Always move DOM focus into the popup list
Never restore focus because the browser handles every case
mcqs.explanation: The bank distinguishes reusable focus mechanics from pattern-specific semantics. Option 0 couples unlike widgets; option 2 is wrong for the combobox model; and restoration must be deliberately handled when the opener still exists.

mcqs.question: Which state is the best candidate for URL synchronization in a revisitable paginated table?
options: Row hover state
A pending request flag
Page and user-meaningful filters
The currently focused button's DOM node
mcqs.explanation: Page and filters describe a navigable, shareable view and support Back/Forward behavior. Hover, pending work, and a DOM node are transient implementation state and should remain local.

mcqs.question: In D3, what does a key function passed to selection.data() give you?
options: Object constancy: elements follow their datum by identity across updates instead of by index
Faster canvas rendering for large datasets
Automatic axis ticks and gridlines
An exit selection ordered by the new data
mcqs.explanation: With a key function, data joins match elements to datums by identity, so re-sorted data moves existing elements instead of rebinding them; without it, joins happen by index and elements 'jump'.

scenarios.prompt: In a 45-minute round, turn this partial editable autocomplete into a race-safe controlled component. Keep input focus in the input, expose the active option, cancel obsolete work, and handle keyboard acceptance.

code.code: type Option = { id: string; label: string }; type Props = { value: string; onChange: (value: string) => void; search: (query: string, signal: AbortSignal) => Promise<Option[]> }; function Autocomplete({ value, onChange, search }: Props) { /* TODO: state, effect cleanup, ARIA, keyboard */ return <input value={value} onChange={e => onChange(e.target.value)} />; }

scenarios.modelAnswer: Keep `value` controlled by the caller and store only derived or transient state locally: `open`, `options`, `activeId`, and request status. In an effect keyed by `value`, clear the prior timer and abort the prior controller in cleanup; after the debounce, call `search` with the signal and apply results only for the current request. Ignore abort failures and expose real errors. Render the input with `role=combobox`, `aria-expanded`, `aria-controls`, and `aria-activedescendant`; render the popup as a listbox with options. Down Arrow changes the active option, Enter commits it and closes, and Escape closes without inventing a new value. Do not intercept normal text editing keys.
rubric: Preserves a controlled input with synchronous `onChange` behavior
Cancels both debounce work and the obsolete request, with stale-result protection
Implements the combobox/listbox ARIA relationships and input focus model
Handles Down Arrow, Enter, Escape, empty/loading/error states, and selection coherently
Cleans up effects and avoids duplicated derived state

scenarios.prompt: Implement the behavior layer for a modal component. It must restore focus to the opener, contain keyboard focus, close on Escape, and avoid claiming modal semantics unless outside content is actually inert.

code.code:
type ModalProps = { open: boolean; titleId: string; onClose: () => void; children: React.ReactNode }; function Modal({ open, titleId, onClose, children }: ModalProps) { /* TODO: focus capture, focus cycling, Escape, dialog markup */ if (!open) return null; return
{children}
; }

scenarios.modelAnswer: Capture `document.activeElement` when opening, move focus to an appropriate element inside after mount, and restore focus on close if the opener still exists; otherwise choose a logical workflow target. Add `aria-modal="true"` only when the application also prevents interaction with and visually obscures the rest of the page. Handle Escape and a visible close button. For Tab and Shift+Tab, find the current tabbable descendants and wrap at the two ends; if there are none, focus a static dialog element with `tabIndex={-1}`. Register and remove the key listener in an effect cleanup, and ensure nested ownership is defined rather than allowing multiple dialogs to fight over the listener.
rubric: Moves focus inside on open and restores it safely on close
Contains Tab and Shift+Tab without using positive tabindex values
Implements Escape, a visible close control, and accessible dialog naming
Coordinates actual outside inertness with `aria-modal` instead of relying on the attribute alone
Cleans up listeners and handles missing opener or empty-content edge cases

scenarios.prompt: Build a fixed-height virtualized list for stable-height rows. The interviewer will scroll rapidly and select a row by stable ID. Explain how you would preserve keyboard access and avoid mounting every item.

code.code:
type Row = { id: string; label: string }; type Props = { rows: Row[]; height: number; rowHeight: number }; function VirtualList({ rows, height, rowHeight }: Props) { /* TODO: visible window, overscan, positioning, selection */ return
{rows.map(row =>
{row.label}
)}
; }

scenarios.modelAnswer: Use a scroll container with a spacer whose height is `rows.length * rowHeight`, then derive the first visible index from `scrollTop`, the last index from viewport height, and a small overscan range. Render only that slice, absolutely position each row using the stable row index, and attach the supplied row height and width through inline positioning styles. Keep selection keyed by `row.id`, not by the recycled DOM node or array position. Expose a keyboard path that can move the active ID and scroll the corresponding row into view. Measure scrolling before adding this complexity, and provide loading and an accessible fallback when the interaction model cannot safely be virtualized.
rubric: Renders a visible window plus limited overscan rather than the full dataset
Uses a spacer and deterministic row positioning for stable-height rows
Uses stable item IDs for selection and does not confuse recycled nodes with identity
Keeps keyboard navigation and scroll-to-item behavior reachable
Explains trade-offs, loading behavior, and when a non-virtualized fallback is safer

scenarios.prompt: This dashboard updates its chart in place when the data refreshes. Bars jump around after re-sorting and tooltips show values from the previous data. Review the rendering code and fix the model.
scenarios.modelAnswer: The join is by index: data() without a key binds the first datum to the first element, so when the array re-sorts, each rect keeps its position and receives a different datum — that is why bars jump and tooltips show values from the previous data. Give each datum a stable identity and join by key: .data(data, d => d.id); then use enter for new elements, update for both (merged via selection.join), and exit for removed ones, computing x from the data’s sorted position rather than the array index. Keep transitions inside the enter/update/exit functions so re-sorts animate to the new positions. While there, check accessibility — aria labels or a tabular fallback for screen readers — and measure rendering when the series grows.
rubric: Identifies join-by-index as the cause of the jumping bars and stale tooltips
Adds a key function to selection.data for object constancy and uses enter/update/exit (or selection.join)
Derives positions from the data instead of array indexes, with transitions per selection
Adds accessibility (labels or tabular fallback) and considers rendering cost as data grows
